Subject: Net terms matrix & VAT responsibility mapping

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — good conversation and excited about the pilot with Lumencare. To make the procurement conversation concrete for your finance team, I attached a simple Net Terms matrix (NetTermsMatrix_v1.xlsx) that lays out our standard options and what we ask for on our side for each. High level:

- Net30: standard for established customers (no deposit), requires completed vendor setup + signed order.
- Net45: available for 60–90 day pilots with milestone invoicing or a small upfront deposit (25%).
- Net60: granted only after a formal credit evaluation and a 1–3 month track record (or an approved corporate guarantee); we usually pair this with a credit limit and additional VAT documentation for cross-border billing.

On VAT: we map responsibility by billing entity and region in the sheet. For UK/EU customers we need a VAT registration number or a reverse-charge confirmation; for US customers we issue invoices net of VAT but will collect any applicable state taxes if you provide exemption certificates.

Given Lumencare’s timeline, a pragmatic path often works best: pilot on Net45 with a 25% up-front, then move to Net60 after two on-time cycles + a quick credit check. If that sounds acceptable I can loop finance/legal and push a tailored PO/terms to DocuSign.

Attachments: NetTermsMatrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

Next steps: can you confirm whether procurement needs Net60 on day one, or if Net45 for the pilot is acceptable? Also please share the PO number if available.

Best,

Kimberly Park

Hi Kimberly,

Appreciate the clear matrix. Lumencare’s procurement policy prefers Net60 for any third-party vendors, even for pilots — that’s our baseline for vendor onboarding. I understand Redwood’s credit checks; our finance team is OK with providing a PO immediately (attached) and a VAT registration certificate (we’re UK-registered, VAT ID attached).

Two asks on our side:
1) Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept Net60 during the pilot if a PO is provided and Lumencare commits to a 50% deposit on the first invoice?
2) We need an explicit statement in your invoice that shows VAT handling (who is responsible) since our AP requires that for cross-border payments.

I attached our PO: PO_4567_Lumencare.pdf (PDF, 120KB). If the deposit requirement is a blocker, call me and we’ll figure a workaround.

Thanks,

Subject: Fwd: Net terms matrix & VAT responsibility mapping (internal)

Kim / Lauren — forwarding Sarah’s note. Quick rundown from finance perspective:

- We can entertain Net60 for pilot if we get stronger commercial protections up front. Recommended conditional terms: 50% deposit on first invoice OR a 15% non-refundable pilot fee + PO + signed SOW.
- Credit limit: propose $250k initial cap for Lumencare, reassess after two billing cycles.
- VAT: require either VAT registration (provided) OR a reverse-charge self-assessment from the buyer for EU/UK billed entities. Lumencare says they are UK-registered; ask for the registered VAT number and a scanned certificate (they attached one).
- Approvals: Legal needs a short amendment stating the deposit and credit cap; accounting needs vendor setup form completed. I attached our credit evaluation template for completeness.

Attachments: credit-eval-template.docx (docx, 32KB)

If we move forward with the 50% deposit + PO, we can approve Net60 for the pilot and fast-track vendor setup. Without deposit, we should push for Net45 and milestone invoicing.

– Priyom
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Net terms matrix & VAT responsibility mapping

Hi Sarah — thanks for the PO and VAT certificate. I spoke to Priyom and legal this morning. Proposed path that will keep procurement happy and get the pilot running quickly:

1) Pilot terms: Net45 with a 50% upfront deposit on the first invoice, remainder Net45 after delivery.
2) Conditional Net60: Redwood will convert to Net60 after two consecutive on-time payments and a light credit check (we’ll use the credit-eval-template). At that point we’ll set an initial credit limit of $250K.
3) VAT/invoice language: our invoices will state ‘VAT to be handled by buyer under reverse-charge’ if Lumencare confirms reverse-charge applies; otherwise Redwood will bill VAT and Lumencare will reimburse. We’ll include this clause in the DocuSign amendment.

I’ve generated the DocuSign request here: https://docusign.com/req/XYZ-123 — it includes the PO and the deposit schedule. If you can sign and return, accounting will kick off vendor setup and we’ll issue the first invoice for the deposit.

Attachments: NetTermsMatrix_v1.xlsx (revised copy, 52KB)

If anything in the amendment is a blocker for Lumencare’s legal team, point them to our legal contact at legal@redwoodinference.com and we’ll iterate quickly.

Best,

Kimberly
